video_title: What was it REALLY like coaching Rudy Gay and Zach Randolph 👀

quotes.speaker: Lionel Hollins
quotes.summary_phrase: Lionel Hollins on his transition to coaching after playing
quotes.excerpt: I actually went back to school and while I was getting my degree, I volunteered at Arizona State.

text_blocks.speaker: Tony Allen
text_blocks.text: When the coaching thing did it come full circle to you or did you fight it a little bit first?

text_blocks.speaker: Lionel Hollins
text_blocks.text: I actually went back to school and while I was getting my degree, I volunteered at Arizona State. Then I went and tried to get a job and everybody looked at me like I was stupid. I'm 31 and the jobs that I was applying for were entry-level jobs because I had no experience working and I tell them.

quotes.social_post: Lionel Hollins shares that he struggled to find work after his playing career ended, even getting rejected for entry level jobs and being told he was not qualified to work at a car dealership.

quotes.speaker: Lionel Hollins
quotes.summary_phrase: Lionel Hollins on his difficult job search after his playing career
quotes.excerpt: I tried to get on with ESPN and the guy told me, you don't have enough experience.
quotes.quote: I tried to get on with ESPN and the guy told me, you don't have enough experience for this job. You have enough experience, no experience and we need to put you in that job. And then he didn't hire me. And that was cool. The most embarrassing and humiliating thing that I tried, one of my buddies worked for a car dealership in Portland and he said, man, come on down, you can sell cars, you know people. I come down and I meet with the sales manager and he said, yeah, I just need you to meet with the general manager, I got a job for you. I go up and meet with the general manager and the general manager is like, we don't give away cars free here. I said, I understand that. He says, we are here to make money. What makes you think you can sell cars? I said, well, I know a lot of people and if I believe in something, I can sell it.
quotes.social_post: Lionel Hollins recalls the humiliation of trying to sell cars after his NBA career, noting that a general manager once questioned his ability to sell anything at all.

quotes.speaker: Lionel Hollins
quotes.summary_phrase: Lionel Hollins on joining the Arizona State coaching staff
quotes.excerpt: Cotton Fitzsimmons and Jerry Colangelo called me, asked me if I wanted to be assistant coach.
quotes.quote: Next year I went back to ASU and then the next year, Cotton Fitzsimmons and Jerry Colangelo called me, asked me if I wanted to be assistant coach with them and I said, certainly. I was there seven years, we averaged 57 wins a year. We went to the finals with Barkley, had Tom Chambers, had Danny Manning, and we had Kevin Johnson, I can't leave out Dan Majerle.
quotes.social_post: Lionel Hollins reflects on his early coaching days as an assistant with the Suns, working with stars like Charles Barkley, Kevin Johnson, and Dan Majerle during a successful seven year run.

quotes.speaker: Lionel Hollins
quotes.summary_phrase: Lionel Hollins on his initial approach to coaching
quotes.excerpt: When I started, it was just a job. I couldn't get a job anywhere else.
quotes.quote: When I started, it was just a job. I couldn't get a job anywhere else and I knew basketball. But when I started coaching, I really knew I knew basketball. I knew what it took to win, how to put together a team, how to communicate, motivate.
quotes.social_post: Lionel Hollins says he initially viewed coaching as just a job because he could not find work elsewhere, but eventually realized he had a deep understanding of how to motivate and lead a team.

quotes.speaker: Lionel Hollins
quotes.summary_phrase: Lionel Hollins on his coaching style and communication
quotes.excerpt: I yell, but also hug. I also talk.
quotes.quote: I yell, but also hug. I also talk. You and Zach were going through the jogging up and down at start of practice and I just said, yo, is that the fastest you can do that? Zach said, nah. And so y'all started running. I didn't yell at him and I didn't yell at you because if I yell, y'all would be all over me. But what I told Zach one time, he may not remember, I said, Zach, I know there's days you don't want to practice. I don't know why, but I know there's days that you don't want to practice. And I said, if you don't want to practice, just tell me. Because Z-Bo was way up here. I could give Z-Bo a day off and not feel bad about it. And so, I said, but if you practice, you got to practice hard. You don't mess up my practice.
quotes.social_post: Lionel Hollins shares his coaching philosophy with Zach Randolph, telling him that if he did not want to practice, he could just say so, but if he chose to participate, he had to work hard.

quotes.speaker: Lionel Hollins
quotes.summary_phrase: Lionel Hollins on coaching star players with high standards
quotes.excerpt: All the stars were tough. They were demanding of you and of themselves.
quotes.quote: All the stars were tough. They were demanding of you and of themselves. So, you know, they're hard. They want something and they really believe in it. It's like now all the guys that want you to go and review something. You know blaten well that they nobody touched you. You just fell on the floor and rolled over. Now you want us to review. Man, get up off the floor. But you know, sometimes you got to be open and I learned to be, all my coaches, and Jack Ramsey had a lot of influence on me even after I quit playing. And he said, be on time, run practices and stop them on time, start them on time, end them on time. And he says, fundamentals first, and he says, demand high standards. And that's what it's about.
quotes.social_post: Lionel Hollins calls out modern players for flopping and asking for reviews, saying that back in his day, he would tell players to just get up off the floor.

quotes.speaker: Lionel Hollins
quotes.summary_phrase: Lionel Hollins on Zach Randolph's impact and work ethic
quotes.excerpt: Rudy don't get a lot of credit for the success we had, but Rudy was a big part.
quotes.quote: Rudy don't get a lot of credit for the success we had, but Rudy was a big part of our success. Man, he could get 40 on Carmelo, LeBron, and he'd guard both of them. KD, all those guys didn't want to see him on a regular basis. Not when he was healthy. And so, the day they didn't think he was deserving of the money, but there's a lot of people today that aren't deserving of the money, but they still get it. And so, I have to give Rudy his kudos.
quotes.social_post: Lionel Hollins gives Rudy Gay his flowers, noting that when healthy, Gay could score 40 on stars like LeBron and KD and was a massive part of their team success.
